$why: A skipped `describe` reports as a passing file, so the runner cannot tell you it stopped running. Every entry here is a suite that is skipped on purpose; the reason has to say what would have to change for it to run, because `waiting on ISS-214's endpoints` is what the device-runner E2E said for months after those endpoints shipped — and when the flag was finally set on 2026-08-25 it failed on the first line. A reason that cannot expire is not a reason.

declared.packages/core/tests/integration/memory-l: Asserts real pgvector ranking against a live embeddings provider (EMBEDDINGS_BASE_URL + EMBEDDINGS_API_KEY). Not a missing-wiring skip: giving CI those credentials would put a paid third-party call on every PR, and a stubbed provider would assert the stub. Run it by hand against a real endpoint when touching packages/core/src/memory/embeddings.
declared.packages/core/src/integrations/google/li: Reaches Google's real token endpoint and a real spreadsheet, so it runs only with GOOGLE_TEST_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON and GOOGLE_TEST_SPREADSHEET_ID set. Not a missing-wiring skip: every other Google test asserts what Forge SENT against a recorded boundary, and no fixture can prove Google accepts the assertion, which is what ISS-1036's rule 'test-connection must actually mint a token against Google and read something with it' asks for. It ends the moment a service account and a spreadsheet shared with it exist for this deployment — asked for as the question record on ISS-1036. Until then the file's second describe fails unless both variables are ABSENT, so this declaration cannot outlive the credential arriving.
